name: AcousticBass
tagline: Wavetable bass synth with upright and electric tones
description: An 8-voice bass instrument built on two fixed additive wavetables, one for upright and one for electric bass. Each note sums a part that holds while the key is down with a brighter part that fades away, plus an optional noise click at the start, through a one-pole low-pass tone control. Nothing is physically modelled or sampled; use it for simple synthesized bass lines.

features.name: Bass Type
features.description: Upright uses a five-partial wavetable weighted to the fundamental; Electric uses six partials with stronger upper harmonics.

features.name: Play Style
features.description: Fingered, Picked and Slapped set how loud the fading attack part starts (0.7, 1.0 or 1.3 times velocity) against the held part.

features.name: Decay
features.description: Sets how quickly the attack part fades while the note is held; the held part sustains until note-off.

features.name: Fret Noise
features.description: Adds a white-noise burst about 2 ms long at the start of each note, scaled by the 0-1 Fret Noise amount.

features.name: Tone
features.description: A one-pole low-pass whose cutoff rises with the 0-1 Tone control, from dark to nearly open.

name: AI Producer
tagline: Plays a fixed 72-bar house arrangement as MIDI, synced to the host
description: Pressing Generate builds a 72-bar house arrangement in A minor (drums, bass, a two-note chord part and a lead in the drops) and plays it out as MIDI along the host timeline from bar 1. The prompt box is shown but not used: the AI client is a stub, so every prompt produces the same track. This is the plugin in plugins/AIProducer, separate from the AIProducer Ableton Remote Script in ableton/remote-scripts/AIProducer.

features.name: Fixed Arrangement
features.description: Intro 8, build 8, drop 16, breakdown 8, build 8, drop 16 and outro 8 bars; the track is written for 128 BPM but plays at the host tempo.

features.name: Drums and Bass
features.description: Drums on channel 10 (kick 36 on every beat, snare 38 on 2 and 4, closed hat 42 on eighths) and bass on channel 1 repeating MIDI note 45 (A) on every quarter note.

features.name: Chords and Lead
features.description: Channel 2 holds A and E (notes 69 and 76) for every bar, and channel 3 plays an ascending eighth-note run on major-pentatonic steps above A in every other bar of the drops.

features.name: Transport-Following Playback
features.description: Events are placed by host PPQ position, and sounding notes are released when the transport stops, loops or jumps.

features.name: MIDI-Only Output
features.description: It clears the audio passing through it and drops incoming MIDI, outputting only the notes it generates.

name: AnalogKick
tagline: Sine kick drum with pitch sweep, noise click and drive
description: A kick drum synthesizer: a sine wave whose pitch drops from above the base pitch, a 5 ms noise click, tanh drive and a fixed low-pass. Any MIDI note triggers the same kick, with velocity setting the level. The sound is generated digitally; nothing in the code emulates analog circuitry.

features.name: Pitch and Pitch Envelope
features.description: Base pitch 20-200 Hz (default 55 Hz); Pitch Env 0-4 starts the note up to five times higher and Pitch Decay (1-200 ms) sets how fast it falls.

features.name: Decay
features.description: Exponential amplitude decay from 10 ms to 2 s.

features.name: Click
features.description: Mixes in a white-noise burst that fades over about 5 ms, for the beater attack.

features.name: Drive
features.description: Gain of 1-10 into a tanh soft clipper, for a rounder or more distorted kick.

features.name: Tone
features.description: Lowers the sine body by up to half relative to the click; it is a balance control, not a filter.

name: AutoPanner
tagline: LFO auto-panner and tremolo with stereo width control
description: A stereo effect that moves the left and right channel gains with a free-running LFO, using an equal-power gain law. The Phase Offset between the two channels decides the effect: at 0 the channels move in opposition for a left-right pan, and at the default 0.5 they rise and fall together, which sounds as a tremolo. A mid/side width control is applied before the movement.

features.name: Waveform
features.description: Sine, Triangle or Square LFO; the square switches hard between positions.

features.name: Rate and Depth
features.description: Rate from 0.01 to 20 Hz, not synced to tempo; Depth 0-1 sets how far the gains swing.

features.name: Phase Offset
features.description: Phase between the left and right LFOs from 0 to 1 cycle; 0 gives auto-pan and 0.5 gives tremolo.

features.name: Stereo Width
features.description: Scales the side signal from 0 (mono) to 2 (twice as wide) before panning.

name: BasicSynth
tagline: 8-voice subtractive synth with filter, effects and four patches
description: An 8-voice subtractive synthesizer: one oscillator (sine, saw or square), an ADSR amp envelope, and a multi-mode filter per voice, followed by saturation, chorus and reverb. It comes with Init, Bass, Pad and Lead patches, offered to the host as programs.

features.name: Oscillator
features.description: Sine, sawtooth or square, with note velocity setting the level

features.name: ADSR envelope
features.description: Attack and decay 1 ms to 2 s, release 1 ms to 5 s, sustain 0 to 1; linear segments

features.name: Multi-mode filter
features.description: Low-pass, high-pass, band-pass or notch state-variable filter; cutoff 20 Hz to 20 kHz, resonance (Q) 0.5 to 10

features.name: Effects
features.description: Saturation (soft clip, hard clip or tube) into a stereo chorus into a Schroeder-style reverb, each with its own mix

features.name: Factory patches
features.description: Init, Bass, Pad and Lead, chosen from a menu or from the host's program list

features.name: 8-voice polyphony
features.description: Round-robin voice stealing when a ninth note arrives

useCases: Bass - start from the Bass patch: dark low-pass, short release, a little tube drive
Pads - start from the Pad patch: slow attack and release, chorus and a large room
Leads - start from the Lead patch: square wave with chorus and some reverb
Learning synthesis - change one control at a time and listen
learningFocus: Polyphonic voice management and voice stealing
A serial effects chain (saturation, chorus, reverb)
Factory patches exposed as host programs

algorithms.name: ADSR Envelope
algorithms.description: Linear attack to 1.0, linear decay to the sustain level, linear release from wherever the note was released

algorithms.name: Voice Stealing
algorithms.description: Round-robin voice allocation when all 8 voices are active

name: BassLine
tagline: Bass-line pattern generator with a built-in bass synth
description: Generates a 4-bar bass pattern over a fixed I-IV-V-I progression in one of seven styles and plays it with its own synth, looped in time with the host transport. It ignores incoming MIDI and outputs no MIDI; the Export MIDI button saves the pattern as a .mid file. Settings are not saved with the project.

features.name: Seven Styles
features.description: Rock, Funk, Jazz, EDM, Reggae, Latin and Blues are rule-based patterns of roots, fifths and chord tones, with small random timing and velocity changes on all but EDM.

features.name: Key, Scale and Octave
features.description: Choose the root key, major or minor (which only changes the Jazz chord tones) and an octave of C1, C2 or C3.

features.name: Bass Synth
features.description: 8-voice Sine, Saw, Square or Triangle oscillator with ADSR and a one-pole low-pass from 100 to 2000 Hz.

features.name: Delay and Reverb
features.description: A 250 ms delay with fixed 30% feedback and a JUCE reverb, each with a 0-1 mix control.

features.name: MIDI Export
features.description: Writes the current pattern to a .mid file on channel 1 at 120 BPM.

name: BrassSection
tagline: Wavetable brass synth: trumpet, trombone and sax with articulations
description: A 12-voice brass instrument that plays fixed additive wavetables for trumpet, trombone and saxophone through a low-pass filter that opens as the note gets louder. Articulation modes, breath noise, vibrato and detuned section copies shape each note. The tones are synthesized from harmonic recipes, not modelled or sampled.

features.name: Instrument
features.description: Trumpet, Trombone or Saxophone, each a single-cycle wavetable with its own harmonic balance.

features.name: Articulation
features.description: Sustain; Staccato, which releases after 150 ms; Marcato, a faster attack with a 30% boost over the first 50 ms; and Fall-off, which drops the pitch 5 semitones over 0.35 s as the note releases.

features.name: Brightness and Expression
features.description: Low-pass cutoff of 500-4500 Hz from Brightness, plus up to 3 kHz more as the level rises; the mod wheel (CC1) sets expression, scaling both level and brightness.

features.name: Breath Noise and Vibrato
features.description: Low-passed noise that follows the note level, and vibrato of up to 3% pitch at 4-8 Hz.

features.name: Section Size
features.description: Plays 1-4 slightly detuned copies of each note (up to 0.7% apart) for a section sound.

name: ChordGenius
tagline: Four-chord progression templates with MIDI file export
description: Shows a four-chord progression built from one of eight genre templates in C major and saves it as a .mid file. It does not produce MIDI in real time: the processor passes incoming MIDI through unchanged, and nothing is saved with the project. It is built as a MIDI effect (IS_MIDI_EFFECT TRUE), so Ableton Live will not load it.

features.name: Genre Templates
features.description: Pop, Rock, Jazz, Blues, EDM, Emotional, Happy and Sad map to fixed Roman-numeral progressions; a parsing bug currently turns every IV chord into a V.

features.name: Triads in C Major
features.description: Each chord is a root-position major or minor triad built on the C major scale; there is no key selector.

features.name: MIDI File Export
features.description: Writes the four chords one bar each on channel 1 at velocity 100, with a 120 BPM tempo marker.

name: ChorusFlanger
tagline: Chorus and flanger from one LFO-modulated delay line
description: A chorus and flanger built on a modulated delay line per channel, with a sine or triangle LFO. Chorus sweeps around 15 ms and flanger around 3 ms; feedback, mix and an offset between the left and right LFOs shape the result. A display shows the LFO and where each channel is on it.

features.name: Two modes
features.description: Chorus (15 ms base delay, up to ±10 ms sweep) and Flanger (3 ms base delay, up to ±2.5 ms sweep)

features.name: Rate and LFO shape
features.description: 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz, skewed toward slow rates; sine or triangle

features.name: Depth
features.description: 0% to 100% of the mode's sweep range

features.name: Stereo Width
features.description: Offsets the right LFO from the left by 0° to 180°

features.name: Feedback and Mix
features.description: Feedback 0% to 95% in both modes; mix 0% to 100% wet

features.name: LFO display and meters
features.description: Draws the LFO with left (orange) and right (cyan) phase markers, plus input and output peak readouts

useCases: Vocal thickening - Chorus with slow rate (0.3-0.8 Hz) and medium depth
Guitar widening - Chorus with Stereo Width at 75-100%
Sweeping pads - Flanger at 1-3 Hz with high feedback
Jet flanging - Flanger with fast rate, high feedback and high depth
Subtle thickness - Chorus with 20-30% depth and 30% mix
learningFocus: Circular delay buffer with write position tracking

algorithms.name: LFO Generation
algorithms.description: Sine and triangle waveforms for smooth and linear modulation

algorithms.name: Fractional Delay Interpolation
algorithms.description: Linear interpolation between samples for smooth pitch changes

algorithms.name: Modulated Delay
algorithms.description: LFO modulates delay time for pitch variation

algorithms.name: Feedback Processing
algorithms.description: Feedback creates comb filtering for flanger resonance

algorithms.name: Stereo Phase Offset
algorithms.description: Independent L/R LFO phases create stereo movement

name: Classic Monosynth
tagline: Three-oscillator mono synth with ladder-style filter and glide
description: A single-voice subtractive synth: saw, pulse and triangle oscillators into a 4-pole ladder-style low-pass filter, with separate filter and amp envelopes, two LFOs and glide. Use it for monophonic bass and lead lines. Note velocity is ignored.

features.name: Three Oscillators
features.description: Saw, pulse (width 0.01-0.99) and triangle, each with its own level; oscillators 2 and 3 detune by up to 24 semitones either way, and oscillator 2 can hard-sync to oscillator 1.

features.name: Ladder-Style Filter
features.description: A four-stage tanh low-pass with cutoff from 20 Hz to 20 kHz, resonance 0-1 and envelope amount of -5000 to +5000 Hz.

features.name: Two ADSR Envelopes
features.description: Filter and amp envelopes with attack and decay up to 2 s and release up to 5 s.

features.name: Two LFOs
features.description: LFO 1 adds vibrato of up to 2 semitones and LFO 2 modulates pulse width, each at 0.1-20 Hz.

features.name: Glide
features.description: Slides between notes over 0-2 s.

name: CleanDelay
tagline: Stereo delay up to 2 seconds with feedback and ping-pong
description: A stereo delay built on a circular buffer, with delay time from 1 ms to 2 s, feedback up to 99%, and a wet/dry mix. Ping-pong mode feeds the left delay line into the right channel's feedback. Input and output meters show levels.

features.name: Delay Time
features.description: 1 ms to 2 s, with the knob skewed toward short times

features.name: Feedback
features.description: 0% to 99%, shown as a percentage

features.name: Mix
features.description: 0% (dry) to 100% (wet), shown as a percentage

features.name: Ping-Pong
features.description: The right channel's feedback is taken from the left delay line instead of its own

features.name: Meters
features.description: Input and output level meters

useCases: Vocal slapback - quick doubling (80-120 ms, low feedback)
Eighth-note echo - 250 ms at 120 BPM
Long ambient echoes - 500-800 ms with high feedback
Haas widening - 10-30 ms, no feedback
Dub-style throws - 375 ms (dotted eighth at 120 BPM), automate Mix
learningFocus: Circular buffer implementation for delay lines
Multi-channel processing with shared write position
Real-time parameter control (delay time, feedback, mix)
Showing a 0-1 parameter as a percentage

algorithms.name: Circular Buffer Delay
algorithms.description: Delay line that wraps its read and write positions around a fixed buffer

algorithms.name: Ping-Pong Feedback
algorithms.description: The right channel takes its feedback from the left delay line

name: DrumMachine
tagline: Self-playing drum pattern generator with five synthesized voices
description: Generates a one-bar, 16-step drum pattern in one of seven styles and plays it with built-in synthesized drums, looped in time with the host transport. It ignores incoming MIDI and outputs no MIDI; Export MIDI saves the pattern as a .mid file. Settings are not saved with the project.

features.name: Seven Styles
features.description: Rock, Hip-Hop, Jazz, EDM, Funk, Latin and Blues patterns, with Complexity 1-10 adding ghost notes and extra hits.

features.name: Five Drum Voices
features.description: Kick (sine sweeping 150 to 50 Hz), snare (200 Hz tone plus noise), tom (120 to 100 Hz), and hi-hat and crash as unfiltered noise bursts with short and long decays.

features.name: Swing and Fills
features.description: Swing only affects the Jazz style, adding off-beat hats above 0.3 rather than shifting timing; Fills only affect Rock, adding a four-step tom run.

features.name: Transport Sync
features.description: Steps follow the host's beat position, with each hit starting at the beginning of the host's audio block.

features.name: MIDI Export
features.description: Writes the pattern on channel 10 with General MIDI notes (36, 38, 42, 47, 49).

name: DrumSynth
tagline: Synthesized kick, snare, clap and hi-hats on the GM drum map
description: A drum synth with five sounds made from oscillators and filtered noise: kick, snare, clap, closed hi-hat and open hi-hat. Notes follow the General MIDI drum map, each hit plays at its own position in the block and at its velocity, and a closed hat chokes an open one.

features.name: Kick
features.description: Sine with a pitch sweep from 3x down to the set pitch (30-100 Hz), plus decay, click, tone and drive

features.name: Snare
features.description: A tuned body mixed with band-passed noise (3.5-6.5 kHz), with tune, snap, tone, decay and mix

features.name: Clap
features.description: Several short bursts of band-passed noise followed by a tail, with tone and decay

features.name: Closed and open hi-hat
features.description: Filtered noise with tune, decay, tone and click; the open hat rings longer, and a closed or pedal hat cuts it off

features.name: GM note map
features.description: C1 kick, D1 snare, D#1 clap, F#1 and G#1 closed hat, A#1 open hat

features.name: Velocity and timing
features.description: Each hit's level follows its velocity, and hits start on their exact sample within the block

useCases: Electronic drum parts programmed on the GM drum map
Drum clips written for other GM instruments, played back unchanged
Layering a synthesized kick or clap under recorded drums
Learning how kicks, snares and hats are built from oscillators and noise

name: ElectricPiano
tagline: Wavetable electric piano with Rhodes, Wurlitzer and hybrid tones
description: A 16-voice electric piano that plays fixed single-cycle wavetables, with a velocity curve, a tone low-pass and per-voice tremolo. Notes hold at a steady level while the key is down and fade after release at a rate set by Decay. The sound is synthesized from wavetables, not modelled or sampled.

features.name: Model
features.description: Rhodes, Wurlitzer, or Hybrid (a 50/50 blend of the two) wavetables.

features.name: Velocity Curve
features.description: Reshapes velocity with a power curve: squared at 0, square root at 0.5 and linear at 1.

features.name: Tone and Decay
features.description: Tone blends in a one-pole low-pass for a darker sound; Decay sets how long notes take to fade after key-up.

features.name: Tremolo
features.description: Amplitude tremolo of up to plus or minus 50% at 0.1-20 Hz.

features.name: Chorus, Reverb and Output Level
features.description: Chorus and Reverb are a one-sample delay blend and a one-pole blend that mostly soften the tone; Output Level runs from -24 to +12 dB.

name: FMSynth
tagline: Four-operator FM synth with eight algorithms
description: A 6-voice FM synthesizer with four sine operators, each with its own level, frequency ratio and ADSR envelope. Eight algorithms connect the operators in different modulator and carrier layouts, and operator 1 can feed back into itself.

features.name: Four sine operators
features.description: Each with level, ratio (0.25 to 16 in steps of 0.25) and its own ADSR envelope

features.name: Eight algorithms
features.description: From four parallel carriers, through pairs and stacks, to a four-operator serial chain

features.name: Feedback
features.description: Operator 1 modulates its own phase, from 0 to 1

features.name: Velocity
features.description: Note velocity scales the voice's output level

features.name: 6-voice polyphony
features.description: Six voices, managed by JUCE's Synthesiser

useCases: Electric piano tones - a modulator at ratio 1 into a carrier, with a fast-decaying modulator envelope
Bell tones - non-integer ratios such as 3.5 for inharmonic partials
FM bass - low ratios and a short modulator envelope
Bright leads - high modulator levels and some feedback

name: FreezeFX
tagline: Spectral freeze that holds a sound's level and pitch
description: FreezeFX passes audio through until you press Freeze, then holds the spectrum it captured, using an STFT with FFT sizes from 1024 to 8192 and 2x, 4x or 8x overlap. Each bin keeps the phase advance measured just after freezing, so the held sound keeps its pitch and level; phase randomization and spectral blur can then animate or smear it.

features.name: Freeze
features.description: Captures the magnitude of every bin and keeps advancing each bin's phase at the rate it was measured, so the held sound stays at the pitch and level it had

features.name: Freeze Mix
features.description: 0% to 100% (default 100%), adding the frozen spectrum to the live one bin by bin

features.name: Phase Random and Phase Speed
features.description: Below 50% a smooth random walk that pulls neighbouring bins together; from 50% up, per-bin sine modulation for denser movement. Speed 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz

features.name: Spectral Blur
features.description: Averages each frozen bin with its neighbours, over 1 to 6 bins

features.name: Status display
features.description: Shows FROZEN or PROCESSING

useCases: Hold a chord or vowel as a sustained pad
Extend the decay of a percussive hit
Drones built from a short sample
Slowly shifting textures with Phase Random and Blur

name: Gate
tagline: Gate and downward expander with hold, range and external key input
description: A noise gate that can also work as a downward expander. It reads its level from the track or, with Sidechain Enable on, from an external key input, using RMS or peak detection. Attack, hold, release, range and up to 10 ms of lookahead shape how it opens and closes.

features.name: Gate and Expander modes
features.description: Gate drops the signal by the full Range below the threshold; Expander turns it down by the Ratio (1:1 to 20:1), never further than Range

features.name: Threshold and Range
features.description: Threshold -60 dB to 0 dB; Range -96 dB to 0 dB sets how far the gate closes

features.name: Attack, Hold and Release
features.description: Attack 0.1-100 ms, hold 0-1000 ms, release 10-1000 ms

features.name: Lookahead
features.description: Delays the audio by 0 ms to 10 ms behind the detector so the gate is open when a transient arrives

features.name: Key input and detection
features.description: Optional external sidechain input for detection; RMS (1-50 ms window) or peak detection, linked across both channels

features.name: Meters
features.description: Input level and gain reduction meters

useCases: Reduce cymbal bleed on close-miked kick and snare
Mute amp noise between guitar phrases
Gentle expansion to lower breaths and room noise between vocal lines
Key a gate from another track through the sidechain input

name: GranularEngine
tagline: Real-time granular effect on the last 10 seconds of input
description: GranularEngine records its input into a 10-second buffer and plays it back as overlapping grains, up to 64 at a time. You set grain size, density, scan speed, read position, pitch, spray, reverse probability and stereo spread, and choose one of six grain windows. MIDI notes, when present, scale grain density by velocity.

features.name: Grain controls
features.description: Size 10-500 ms, density 1-100 grains per second, pitch -24 to +24 semitones

features.name: Scan Speed and Position
features.description: Scan Speed (0.25x to 4x) sets how fast grains move through the input; Position sets where in the buffer they read from

features.name: Spray, Reverse and Stereo Width
features.description: Spray scatters each grain's start point; Reverse is the chance a grain plays backwards; Stereo Width (0-200%) spreads grains at random across the stereo field

features.name: Six windows
features.description: Hann, Gaussian, Triangle, Tukey, Blackman and Kaiser, with a Shape control for Gaussian width and Tukey taper

features.name: Displays
features.description: Waveform of the 10-second buffer with the read position, a preview of the window, and grain activity, redrawn 60 times a second

features.name: Velocity-scaled density
features.description: While a MIDI note is held, grain density is multiplied by its velocity

useCases: Turn a sustained vocal or instrument into a grain cloud
Stutter and glitch textures with short grains and high spray
Slow, smeared versions of the input with Scan Speed below 1x
Octave-shifted textures with Pitch at ±12 semitones
Backwards-sounding textures with Reverse near 100%

name: HiHat
tagline: Noise hi-hat synth with band-pass tone and open/closed decay
description: A hi-hat voice made from white noise filtered to a high band, shaped by an exponential decay and soft-clipped. Any MIDI note triggers the same hat, with velocity setting the level; there is no open/closed choke between notes.

features.name: Band-Pass Noise
features.description: Three high-pass and three low-pass one-pole stages keep the noise between a 4-8 kHz lower edge (set by Tone) and 12 kHz.

features.name: Decay
features.description: Decay time from 10 to 500 ms.

features.name: Openness
features.description: Lengthens the decay by up to 2 times, from closed toward open.

features.name: Metallic
features.description: Raises the level into a tanh saturator by up to 3 times for a harder, more saturated hat; it adds no metallic oscillators.

name: Koto
tagline: Plucked-string koto synth using a delay-line string model
description: An 8-voice plucked-string instrument: a noise burst excites a tuned delay-line (comb filter) string, which then passes through a tone low-pass and three body-resonance peaks. The string loop has no damping filter, so all harmonics decay at the same rate. The Scale parameter (In-sen, Hirajoshi, Iwato, Kumoi, Chromatic) is stored but does not yet change the sound.

features.name: Delay-Line String
features.description: A comb filter tuned to the note, with loop feedback from 0.994 to 0.9995 set by Decay (0.1-2).

features.name: Play Style
features.description: Pluck excites the string once, Tremolo re-plucks at the Tremolo Rate (2-20 Hz) and Scrape feeds noise in continuously while the key is held.

features.name: Body Resonance
features.description: Blends in up to 60% of three peaking filters at 250 Hz, 800 Hz and 2 kHz.

features.name: Tone, Attack and Pitch Bend
features.description: A one-pole low-pass for brightness, a 1-100 ms fade-in, and a fixed pitch offset of up to 2 semitones (a parameter, not the MIDI pitch wheel).

name: Limiter
tagline: Lookahead peak limiter with a true-peak warning light
description: A brickwall peak limiter with up to 10 ms of lookahead, so gain comes down before a peak arrives and the output stays under the ceiling. Threshold and auto makeup raise the level into the limiter; release, output trim and meters complete it. A 4x oversampled true-peak check on the output lights a TP indicator when intersample peaks pass 0 dBFS.

features.name: Ceiling
features.description: -12 dB to 0 dB (default -0.3 dB); limiting is linked across both channels, with instant attack

features.name: Lookahead
features.description: 0 ms to 10 ms (default 5 ms), reported to the host as latency; the reduction is held and averaged over the lookahead so it is complete when the peak comes out

features.name: Threshold and Auto Makeup
features.description: With Auto Makeup on, the signal is raised so the threshold level (-24 dB to 0 dB) comes out at the ceiling, up to 12 dB of gain

features.name: Release and Output Trim
features.description: Exponential release 10 ms to 1000 ms; output trim ±12 dB after the limiter

features.name: Meters
features.description: Input, output and gain reduction meters, plus a TP light from a 4x oversampled true-peak check of the output

useCases: Catch peaks on the master bus before export
Raise the level of a mix with Threshold and Auto Makeup
Protect a bus from occasional overs
Check for intersample overs with the TP light

name: Macro Controller
tagline: One macro knob sending up to eight scaled MIDI CC messages
description: Turning the Macro knob sends a MIDI CC message for each enabled target, each with its own CC number, output range and response curve, so one control can move several synth or effect parameters at once. It is built as an audio effect with MIDI output, and it silences any audio passing through it.

features.name: Eight Targets
features.description: Each target has an enable switch and a CC number from 1 to 127; by default targets 1-4 are on, sending CC 1-4.

features.name: Per-Target Range
features.description: Min and Max (0-1) set the span each CC covers, and setting Max below Min inverts it.

features.name: Response Curve
features.description: A power curve from 0.1 to 10 per target: below 1 the CC rises quickly at first, above 1 it rises slowly at first.

features.name: MIDI Channel
features.description: All CCs go out on one selectable channel, 1-16.

features.name: Send on Change
features.description: CCs are sent only when the Macro value moves; changing a target's settings does not resend.

name: MelodyMaker
tagline: Random in-key melody loop played by a built-in synth
description: MelodyMaker generates a four-bar melody in a chosen key (major or natural minor) by a random walk over the scale, then loops it in time with the host transport through its own 8-voice synth. You'd use it to sketch melodic ideas and export the result as a MIDI file. It loads as an instrument, not a MIDI effect: it plays audio and does not send MIDI to other tracks.

features.name: Key and scale
features.description: Twelve root keys and Major or Minor; notes stay within two octaves above the root.

features.name: Transport-synced loop
features.description: The 16-beat melody follows the host's tempo and song position and repeats while the transport plays.

features.name: Built-in synth
features.description: Sine, saw, square or triangle oscillator with an ADSR envelope (attack/decay 1 ms to 2 s, release to 3 s).

features.name: Effects
features.description: Low-pass filter (200 Hz to 20 kHz), a feedback delay and a reverb, each with its own level.

features.name: MIDI file export
features.description: Saves the current melody as a .mid file at 120 BPM in 4/4.

name: MIDI Arpeggiator

parameters.name: Pattern
parameters.range: Up, Down, Up-Down, Down-Up, Random, Played Order

tagline: Tempo-synced arpeggiator for held MIDI notes
description: Turns held chords into a stepped sequence of single notes at a tempo-synced rate, replacing the incoming notes with the arpeggio. Use it on a MIDI track ahead of any instrument to turn sustained chords into rhythmic patterns. Built as a MIDI effect, so Ableton Live will not load it; use a host that accepts third-party MIDI effects.

features.name: Six patterns
features.description: Up, Down, Up-Down, Down-Up, Random and Played Order.

features.name: Rate
features.description: Nine step lengths from 1/1 to 1/32, including 1/4, 1/8 and 1/16 triplets, timed from the host tempo.

features.name: Octave range and gate
features.description: Repeats the pattern over 1 to 4 octaves; Gate sets note length from 0 to 100% of a step.

features.name: Latch
features.description: Keeps the arpeggio running after the keys are released.

features.name: Velocity
features.description: Uses the average velocity of the held notes, or a fixed velocity from 1 to 127.

name: MIDI CC Mapper
tagline: Remaps MIDI CC numbers with range, curve and invert
description: Rewrites incoming MIDI control changes to other CC numbers through eight mapping slots, scaling and shaping the values on the way. Use it to make a controller's knobs drive the CCs a synth expects, or to limit and curve their response. Built as a MIDI effect, so Ableton Live will not load it; use a host that accepts third-party MIDI effects.

features.name: Eight mappings
features.description: Each slot has an enable switch, an input CC and an output CC (1 to 127).

features.name: Output range
features.description: Min and Max scale each mapping's output into a chosen part of the 0 to 127 range.

features.name: Response curve
features.description: Curve raises the value to a power from 0.1 to 10, from a fast rise to a slow one; 1 is linear.

features.name: Invert
features.description: Flips each mapping's value so that a rising control lowers the output.

features.name: Pass-through
features.description: Unmapped CCs and all other MIDI pass through unchanged; a mapped input CC is replaced by its outputs, and several slots can share one input.

name: MIDI Chord Generator

parameters.name: Chord Type
parameters.range: Major, Minor, Dim, Aug, Sus2, Sus4, Maj7, Min7, Dom7, MinMaj7, Dim7, m7b5, Maj6, Min6, Add9, Maj9, Min9, Dom9

parameters.name: Voicing
parameters.range: Root, 1st Inv, 2nd Inv, 3rd Inv, Spread, Drop2, Drop3

tagline: Plays a chord of a chosen type from each incoming note
description: Builds a chord on every incoming note using a fixed chord type and voicing, and releases the whole chord when the note is released. Use it to play full chords from single keys or to turn a bass line into a chord part. Built as a MIDI effect, so Ableton Live will not load it; use a host that accepts third-party MIDI effects.

features.name: 18 chord types
features.description: Triads, sus2/sus4, sixths, sevenths (including dim7 and m7b5) and add9/ninth chords.

features.name: Voicings
features.description: Root position, 1st to 3rd inversion, Spread, Drop-2 and Drop-3.

features.name: Octave shift
features.description: Moves the chord from 2 octaves down to 2 octaves up from the played note.

features.name: Strum
features.description: Offsets each chord note after the first by a set amount; the 0 to 100 value is applied in samples, so the spread is at most a few milliseconds.

features.name: Velocity
features.description: Uses the played velocity or a fixed velocity from 1 to 127.

name: MIDI Groove Quantizer
tagline: Real-time note quantizing with swing and humanize
description: Moves incoming note-ons and note-offs toward a tempo-based grid as they play, with optional swing and random timing and velocity changes. It works without lookahead, so a note can only move within the current audio block, and in practice timing changes are small; velocity humanizing works fully. Built as a MIDI effect, so Ableton Live will not load it; use a host that accepts third-party MIDI effects.

features.name: Grid
features.description: 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, 1/32, 1/8 triplet or 1/16 triplet, from the host tempo.

features.name: Strength
features.description: Moves each note from 0 to 100% of the way to the nearest grid line.

features.name: Swing
features.description: Delays every other grid line by up to half a grid step.

features.name: Humanize timing
features.description: Adds a random offset to note-ons of up to 10% of a grid step.

features.name: Humanize velocity
features.description: Adds a random change of up to plus or minus 30 to note-on velocity.

name: MIDI Harmonizer

parameters.name: Key
parameters.range: C, Db, D, Eb, E, F, Gb, G, Ab, A, Bb, B

parameters.name: Scale
parameters.range: Chromatic, Major, Minor, Dorian, Phrygian, Lydian, Mixolydian, Aeolian, Locrian, Harmonic Minor, Melodic Minor, Pentatonic, Blues

tagline: Adds 3rds, 5ths and octaves above or below each note
description: Passes each incoming note through and adds harmony notes at a third, fifth or octave above or below it. In Chromatic mode the third is a major third and the fifth a perfect fifth; the in-key scale modes are intended to pick diatonic intervals, but their scale lookup currently gives wrong intervals, so check results by ear. Built as a MIDI effect, so Ableton Live will not load it; use a host that accepts third-party MIDI effects.

features.name: Six harmony voices
features.description: Switch on a 3rd, 5th or octave above, and a 3rd, 5th or octave below, in any combination.

features.name: Key and scale
features.description: Twelve keys and 13 scale choices: Chromatic, Major, Minor, the modes, Harmonic and Melodic Minor, Pentatonic and Blues.

features.name: Mix
features.description: Scales the velocity of the harmony notes from 0 to 100%; the original note is always played.

features.name: Velocity
features.description: Harmony notes use the played velocity or a fixed velocity from 1 to 127.

features.name: MIDI learn
features.description: The Mix and Fixed Velocity sliders can be assigned to a MIDI controller.

name: Multiband Compressor
tagline: Four-band compressor with Linkwitz-Riley crossovers
description: A compressor that splits stereo audio into four bands with 24 dB/octave Linkwitz-Riley crossovers and compresses each band with its own settings before summing them back. Each band can be soloed, bypassed, or switched to process mid and side instead of left and right.

features.name: Three crossovers
features.description: 20-500 Hz (default 250 Hz), 200 Hz-5 kHz (default 2 kHz) and 2-16 kHz (default 8 kHz), each a 4th-order Linkwitz-Riley split

features.name: Per-band compression
features.description: Threshold -60 dB to 0 dB, ratio 1:1 to 20:1, attack 0.1-100 ms, release 10-1000 ms, makeup ±12 dB

features.name: Solo and Bypass
features.description: Solo mutes the other bands; Bypass passes a band through uncompressed

features.name: Mid/Side per band
features.description: Encodes the band to mid and side, compresses those with the band's settings, then decodes back to left and right

features.name: Gain reduction meters
features.description: One gain reduction meter per band

useCases: Control low-end dynamics without touching the mids and highs
Compress a harsh upper-mid band on its own
Reduce sibilance by compressing a band set around 4-8 kHz
Learn how crossover splitting and per-band compression interact, one band at a time with Solo

name: OrganEmulator
tagline: Drawbar organ with nine sine drawbars and a rotary-style effect
description: An 8-voice drawbar organ that adds nine sine waves at the standard drawbar footages, in the manner of a tonewheel organ. A simple rotary-speaker effect (pitch wobble from a modulated delay plus tremolo, slow or fast) and a percussion click are applied to each voice.

features.name: 9 drawbars
features.description: 16', 5⅓', 8', 4', 2⅔', 2', 1⅗', 1⅓' and 1', each a sine at that harmonic with a level from 0 to 1

features.name: Rotary-style effect
features.description: A sine LFO moves a short delay (2 ms, up to 5 ms) for pitch wobble and adds tremolo; Slow is 0.7 Hz, Fast is 6 Hz, with Depth and Mix controls

features.name: Percussion click
features.description: A short transient at the start of each note, with level and a decay of 10 ms to 500 ms

features.name: 8-voice polyphony
features.description: Eight voices; velocity sets the note level

useCases: Full organ - most drawbars out with the fast rotary setting
Mellow jazz tones - 16', 8' and 4' only, slow rotary
Bright, thin registrations - upper drawbars with the click up
Learning additive synthesis - hear each harmonic by pulling one drawbar at a time

name: PadSynth
tagline: Unison pad synth with up to 9 detuned oscillators per note
description: A 6-voice pad synth in which every note is a stack of 3 to 9 detuned oscillators spread across the stereo field. A multi-mode filter and a slow-by-default ADSR envelope shape the stack.

features.name: Unison stack
features.description: 3 to 9 oscillators per note (default 7), detuned evenly between minus and plus the Detune amount

features.name: Detune
features.description: 0 to 50 cents (default 10)

features.name: Stereo Width
features.description: Spreads the unison oscillators from centre (0) to fully left and right (1)

features.name: Waveform
features.description: Sine, saw, square or triangle, shared by every oscillator in the stack

features.name: Multi-mode filter
features.description: Low-pass, high-pass, band-pass or notch; cutoff 20 Hz to 20 kHz, resonance 0.5 to 10

features.name: Envelope and polyphony
features.description: ADSR with attack and decay up to 5 s and release up to 10 s (default 0.8 s attack, 1.5 s release); 6-note polyphony; velocity sets the level

useCases: Ambient pads - slow attack, long release, low-pass filter
Supersaw-style chords - saw wave, 7-9 voices, 15-25 cents of detune
Thin, wide textures - sine or triangle with full Stereo Width
Drones - high sustain and long release

name: PanUtil
tagline: Pan, width, gain and mono for one stereo track
description: A track utility for stereo signals: pan or balance, stereo width from mono to 200%, output gain from -36 dB to +24 dB, and a mono switch. All four controls are smoothed, and L/R meters and a pan indicator show the result.

features.name: Pan or Balance
features.description: Pan mode uses a constant-power pan law; Balance mode (the default) only turns the opposite side down, so a centred signal keeps its level

features.name: Width
features.description: Mid/side width from 0% (mono) through 100% (unchanged) to 200%

features.name: Gain
features.description: Output gain from -36 dB to +24 dB; double-click returns it to 0 dB

features.name: Mono
features.description: Sums to mono whatever Width is set to, smoothed so switching does not click

features.name: Meters
features.description: Left and right peak meters and a pan position indicator

useCases: Re-centre a source recorded slightly to one side
Place instruments across the stereo field
Widen a synth or pad with width above 100%
Check mono compatibility with the Mono switch
Trim a track's level without touching the fader
learningFocus: Keeping saved state compatible when parameters are added

algorithms.name: Constant-Power Panning
algorithms.description: Keeps perceived loudness about constant as you pan across the stereo field

algorithms.name: Width Control (M/S Processing)
algorithms.description: Mid/Side processing for stereo width adjustment

name: PhaserFlanger
tagline: Six-stage phaser and short-delay flanger in one
description: A modulation effect with two modes: a phaser built from six all-pass stages with feedback around them, and a flanger built from a modulated 5 to 15 ms delay with feedback. Use it to add sweeping movement to guitars, synths, drums or pads.

features.name: Phaser mode
features.description: Six first-order all-pass stages whose break frequency a sine LFO sweeps up to two octaves either side of Centre Freq (200 Hz to 2 kHz).

features.name: Flanger mode
features.description: An interpolated delay swept between 5 and 15 ms, with its output fed back into the delay line.

features.name: Feedback (-0.9 to 0.9)
features.description: Negative or positive feedback; in phaser mode the wet level is trimmed as feedback rises to hold back the resonant peaks.

features.name: Rate and Depth
features.description: LFO rate from 0.1 to 10 Hz; Depth sets the sweep width in both modes.

features.name: Mix
features.description: Crossfades between the dry and processed signal.

name: PlateReverb
tagline: Simple stereo reverb with size, damping and width
description: A stereo reverb built on JUCE's standard reverb (a Freeverb-style comb and all-pass network), not a model of a plate. Use it for general-purpose room and space on a send or insert.

features.name: Size
features.description: Sets the room size, and with it the decay length.

features.name: Damping
features.description: Sets how quickly high frequencies fade in the tail.

features.name: Width
features.description: Sets the stereo spread of the reverb from mono to full width.

features.name: Mix
features.description: Crossfades from the dry signal at 0 to the reverb alone at 1, scaled so each end keeps its nominal level.

name: Polysynth
tagline: Six-voice saw and square synth with unison
description: A six-voice subtractive synth with a sawtooth and a square oscillator per voice, up to six detuned unison copies, a simple low-pass/high-pass filter and an ADSR envelope. Use it for basic leads, basses and pads.

features.name: Two oscillators
features.description: Saw and square, crossfaded by Osc Mix; the square can be detuned from -24 to +24 semitones.

features.name: Unison
features.description: 1 to 6 stacked copies per voice, spread across up to 50 cents.

features.name: Filter
features.description: One-pole (6 dB/octave) low-pass and high-pass, blended by LP/HP Mix, with cutoff from 20 Hz to 20 kHz.

features.name: ADSR envelope
features.description: Attack and decay up to 2 s, sustain level, release up to 5 s.

features.name: Output Level
features.description: -24 to +12 dB, ramped across each block to avoid clicks.

name: Reverb
tagline: Freeverb-style reverb with pre-delay, width and freeze
description: A Schroeder reverb in the Freeverb layout: 8 parallel damped comb filters and 4 series all-pass filters per channel, with the right channel's combs offset by 23 samples. Controls are room size, damping, width, pre-delay up to 100 ms, mix and freeze.

features.name: 8 parallel comb filters
features.description: Delays of 1116-1617 samples at 44.1 kHz, scaled to the session sample rate

features.name: 4 series all-pass filters
features.description: Delays of 225-556 samples at 44.1 kHz, for diffusion

features.name: Room Size
features.description: 0% to 100%, setting comb feedback from 0.28 to 0.84

features.name: Damping
features.description: One-pole low-pass in each comb's feedback path, darkening the tail as it decays

features.name: Width and Pre-Delay
features.description: Width scales the side signal of the wet output from mono (0%) to full (100%); pre-delay 0 ms to 100 ms

features.name: Freeze
features.description: Sets comb feedback to 1 and stops new input reaching the reverb, so the current tail holds (damping still darkens it)

useCases: Small room ambience - room size 20-30%, damping 60-70%, short pre-delay
Large space - room size 70-90%, damping 30-50%, 20-40 ms pre-delay
Snare reverb - room size 30-40%, short pre-delay, mix 30-40%
Held drones - play a chord, switch Freeze on, and play over the held tail
Subtle room tone - room size 10-20%, high damping, mix 15-25%
learningFocus: Schroeder reverberator topology (parallel combs + series all-pass)
Comb filter tuning to avoid metallic resonances
Damping with one-pole low-pass filter in feedback path
Stereo decorrelation with offset L/R delay lines
Sample rate scaling for delay times

algorithms.name: Comb Filter with Damping
algorithms.description: Parallel comb filters with low-pass damping in feedback path

algorithms.name: All-Pass Filter
algorithms.description: Series all-pass filters for diffusion

algorithms.name: Stereo Processing
algorithms.description: Mono input into separate L/R comb banks, the right one offset by 23 samples, then mid/side width

algorithms.name: Freeze Mode
algorithms.description: Holds the tail by muting the reverb input and setting comb feedback to 1

name: Sampler
tagline: 16-voice sampler with key zones, velocity layers and looping
description: A sampler that loads WAV, AIFF and FLAC files, by file dialog or by dragging them onto the window, and plays them back repitched from each zone's root note. Key zones and velocity layers, with round-robin between samples on the same layer, map samples across the keyboard; amp and filter envelopes and a multi-mode filter shape the sound.

features.name: Sample loading
features.description: WAV, AIFF or FLAC, from a Load Sample dialog or dropped onto the window, listed in a sample browser with memory use

features.name: Key zones and velocity layers
features.description: Zones cover a range of notes with a root note; each zone holds velocity layers, cycling round-robin when several samples match

features.name: Looping
features.description: None, Forward or Ping-Pong per sample, with loop start and end dragged on the waveform display

features.name: Amp and filter envelopes
features.description: Two ADSRs (attack and decay up to 5 s, release up to 10 s); the filter envelope amount runs from -1 to +1

features.name: Multi-mode filter
features.description: Low-pass, high-pass, band-pass or notch; cutoff 20 Hz to 20 kHz, resonance 0.5 to 10

features.name: 16-voice polyphony
features.description: Sixteen voices with master volume; velocity sets the level

useCases: Play a single recorded note across the keyboard
Build a drum kit with one zone per note
Multi-sampled instruments with velocity layers and round-robin
Sustained sounds from short samples with forward or ping-pong loops

name: Saturation
tagline: Five-mode saturation with tone shelves and oversampling
description: A saturation effect with five curves named after hardware (Tape, Tube, Transistor, Transformer, Diode), drive up to 10x, low and high shelves after the curve, dry/wet mix and optional 2x or 4x oversampling. Each mode is a static waveshaping formula, not a circuit model.

features.name: Five modes
features.description: Tape and Transistor are symmetric curves (odd harmonics); Tube, Transformer and Diode treat the two halves of the wave differently, which adds even harmonics

features.name: Drive
features.description: 0% to 100%, multiplying the input by 1x to 10x before the curve

features.name: Oversampling
features.description: Off, 2x or 4x, using JUCE's polyphase IIR half-band filters, to reduce aliasing

features.name: Tone shelves
features.description: Low shelf at 200 Hz and high shelf at 5 kHz, ±12 dB each, after the saturation

features.name: Mix
features.description: 0% (dry) to 100% (saturated) for parallel saturation

features.name: Harmonic display and meters
features.description: Bars for H1-H8 that illustrate the typical harmonic pattern of the mode, scaled by drive (not measured from the audio), plus input and output peak readouts

useCases: Gentle saturation - Tape mode with low drive (10-30%)
Even-harmonic colour - Tube or Transformer mode with medium drive
Harder clipping - Transistor mode with high drive
Strongly lopsided distortion - Diode mode
Parallel saturation - Mix at 30-50%
Less aliasing at high drive - switch on 2x or 4x oversampling
learningFocus: Waveshaping curves named after analog hardware
Shelf filter design for tone shaping

algorithms.name: Tape
algorithms.description: Symmetric soft compression of the level, so it adds odd harmonics

algorithms.name: Tube
algorithms.description: Asymmetric tanh: the positive half saturates harder than the negative

algorithms.name: Transistor
algorithms.description: Linear up to 0.7, then a tanh knee toward 1.0 on both sides

algorithms.name: Transformer
algorithms.description: A gentle cubic term with slightly different gain on each half, then tanh

algorithms.name: Diode
algorithms.description: Clips the positive half from 0.3 upward; the negative half stays linear down to -2

algorithms.name: Oversampling
algorithms.description: Runs the curve and shelves at 2x or 4x the sample rate

name: Shakuhachi
tagline: Breathy flute voice from noise and a tuned delay
description: A four-voice instrument that sends filtered pink noise through a feedback delay line tuned to the note, giving a breathy, flute-like tone. It is a simple delay-line resonator rather than a full physical model of the bamboo tube. Use it for airy lead lines and textures.

features.name: Breath Pressure
features.description: Sets how much noise drives the resonator and how bright that noise is.

features.name: Embouchure (Meri/Kari)
features.description: Shifts the pitch by up to 2 semitones down (meri) or up (kari).

features.name: Air Noise and Brightness
features.description: Air Noise blends unpitched breath noise against the tone; Brightness opens a low-pass filter on the tone.

features.name: Breath attack
features.description: During the attack (10 to 500 ms) the sound fades from breath noise into the tone; release runs from 0.1 to 2 s.

features.name: Vibrato
features.description: Sine vibrato with rate up to 10 Hz and depth up to 5% of the pitch.

name: ShimmerReverb
tagline: Reverb with delayed taps of its own tail
description: A reverb that adds delayed copies of its own tail on top of the main reverb. The code describes these as octave-up and octave-down shimmer, but they are fixed delays of 250 ms and 125 ms with no pitch shift, and the Feedback control only sets how much of them is mixed in. Use it for a longer, echoing reverb tail.

features.name: Size and Damping
features.description: Room size and high-frequency damping of the underlying stereo reverb.

features.name: Shimmer
features.description: Sets the level of the delayed reverb taps.

features.name: Pitch mode
features.description: Up uses the 250 ms tap, Down the 125 ms tap, Both uses both; the taps are not pitch-shifted.

features.name: Feedback (0 to 0.85)
features.description: Blends the tapped signal against the plain reverb; nothing is fed back into the reverb.

features.name: Mix
features.description: Crossfades between the dry input and the processed signal.

name: SimpleComp
tagline: Feed-forward compressor with hard or soft knee
description: A compressor with threshold, ratio, attack, release and a hard or soft knee. Each channel has its own envelope follower, and a fixed makeup gain is added based on threshold and ratio. A meter shows gain reduction.

features.name: Threshold and Ratio
features.description: Threshold -60 dB to 0 dB (default -12 dB), ratio 1:1 to 20:1 (default 4:1)

features.name: Attack and Release
features.description: Attack 0.1 ms to 100 ms, release 10 ms to 1000 ms, both skewed toward short times

features.name: Hard or Soft Knee
features.description: Hard knee, or a 6 dB soft knee with a quadratic transition

features.name: Automatic Makeup Gain
features.description: Adds half the gain reduction a -12 dB signal would get at the current threshold and ratio

features.name: Gain Reduction Meter
features.description: Shows gain reduction over a 0 to 20 dB range

useCases: Even out a vocal performance
Control drum transients and peaks
Add sustain to bass and guitars
Learn how threshold, ratio, attack and release interact
learningFocus: Envelope follower design with attack/release coefficients
Hard vs. soft knee compression curves
Exponential time constants for envelope smoothing
Per-channel state management for stereo processing

algorithms.name: Envelope Follower
algorithms.description: Tracks input level with exponential attack/release coefficients calculated from time parameters

algorithms.name: Soft Knee Gain Reduction
algorithms.description: Gradual transition using a quadratic curve across a 6 dB knee

name: SimpleEQ
tagline: Three-band EQ with switchable high-pass and low-pass filters
description: A three-band EQ: low shelf, mid peak and high shelf, each with frequency and ±12 dB gain, plus a high-pass and a low-pass filter that can be switched in. All five are biquad filters in series; input and output meters show the levels.

features.name: Low Shelf
features.description: 20 Hz to 500 Hz (default 80 Hz), ±12 dB, Q 0.707

features.name: Mid Peak
features.description: 200 Hz to 5 kHz (default 1 kHz), ±12 dB, fixed Q of 1.0

features.name: High Shelf
features.description: 2 kHz to 20 kHz (default 8 kHz), ±12 dB, Q 0.707

features.name: High-Pass Filter
features.description: Off by default; 20 Hz to 500 Hz, 12 dB/octave

features.name: Low-Pass Filter
features.description: Off by default; 2 kHz to 20 kHz, 12 dB/octave

features.name: Meters
features.description: Input and output level meters

useCases: Remove rumble - switch on the HPF at 40-80 Hz
Reduce harshness - cut the mid band at 2-4 kHz by 3-6 dB
Add air - boost the high shelf at 8-12 kHz by 2-4 dB
Telephone effect - HPF at 300 Hz and LPF at 3 kHz
Add weight - boost the low shelf at 80-120 Hz by 3-6 dB
learningFocus: Biquad filter design (shelf, peaking, HPF, LPF)
Recomputing coefficients only when a parameter changes
Cascaded filter processing (5 filters in series)

algorithms.name: Low Shelf Filter
algorithms.description: Bass boost or cut, using the shelf formulas from the RBJ Audio EQ Cookbook (Q=0.707)

algorithms.name: Peaking EQ
algorithms.description: Bell curve for the mid band (Q=1.0)

name: SimpleGain
tagline: Gain control from -60 dB to +12 dB with a peak meter
description: A single gain knob from -60 dB to +12 dB, smoothed so changes do not click, with a peak level meter. It is the smallest plugin in the set and a starting point for learning buffer processing in JUCE.

features.name: Gain
features.description: -60 dB to +12 dB in 0.1 dB steps, default 0 dB (unity)

features.name: Peak meter
features.description: Shows the output peak level, redrawn 30 times a second

features.name: Parameter smoothing
features.description: Gain changes ramp over 50 ms, so moving the knob does not click

features.name: Rotary knob
features.description: One knob with a dB readout below it

name: Sitar
tagline: Plucked-string sitar voice with sympathetic strings
description: A six-voice plucked-string instrument: a noise burst excites a tuned feedback delay (Karplus-Strong), a soft clipper adds bridge buzz, and 13 further tuned delays ring along as sympathetic strings. Use it for sitar-like melodic lines and drones.

features.name: Jawari
features.description: Blends in tanh soft clipping of the string output for a buzzing, brighter tone.

features.name: Sympathetic strings
features.description: 13 resonators fed by the main string, tuned to the played note in a Chromatic, Bhairavi, Yaman or Kafi scale.

features.name: Drone
features.description: Two resonators at C3 and G3, plucked every 4 and 5 seconds, so they are heard only on notes held that long.

features.name: Pitch and vibrato
features.description: Pitch Bend from -2 to +2 semitones and sine vibrato up to 10 Hz and 5% depth.

features.name: Attack
features.description: Fade-in from 1 to 100 ms; the Decay control is read but not used by the engine.

name: SnareSynth
tagline: Synthesized snare from a pitched tone plus noise
description: A synthesized snare drum: a triangle-wave body with a downward pitch sweep, a filtered-noise rattle and a short noise click, mixed and soft-clipped. Any MIDI note triggers the same one-shot hit, scaled by velocity, with up to four overlapping hits.

features.name: Tone
features.description: Body pitch from 100 to 400 Hz.

features.name: Pitch Env
features.description: Starts the body up to three times higher and drops it to Tone over about 30 ms.

features.name: Snappy and Snare Decay
features.description: Level of the noise rattle and its decay time, 10 to 500 ms.

features.name: Decay
features.description: Decay time of the tonal body, 10 ms to 1 s.

features.name: Snap
features.description: Level of a 2 ms noise click at the start of the hit.

name: SpectralFreeze
tagline: STFT spectral freeze with blur, shift, stretch, gate and morph
description: SpectralFreeze runs a 2048-point FFT with a Hann window and 75% overlap, and can hold the current spectrum at the level and pitch it had. Blur, stretch, shift, gate, phase randomize, morph and a low/high cut then reshape the spectrum, frozen or live. A scrolling spectrogram shows the result, and six factory presets demonstrate the effects.

features.name: Freeze
features.description: Holds each bin's magnitude and keeps advancing its phase at the rate measured just after freezing, so the held sound keeps its pitch and level

features.name: Spectral effects
features.description: Blur (Gaussian smoothing over up to 11 bins), Stretch (spreads the spectrum upward by up to 5x), Shift (moves every bin up or down by up to 100 bins), Gate (silences bins below a share of the loudest), Randomize (scrambles phase)

features.name: Morph
features.description: While not frozen, crossfades the live spectrum toward the last frozen one

features.name: Low Cut, High Cut and Dry/Wet
features.description: Zeroes bins outside 20 Hz to 20 kHz limits you set, and blends the processed signal with the dry input

features.name: Spectrogram
features.description: Scrolling display coloured by level from blue to red, with the frozen spectrum overlaid, redrawn 60 times a second

features.name: Six factory presets
features.description: Init, Frozen Blur, Spectral Stretch, Frequency Shifter, Spectral Gate and Granular Texture, plus a quick-save slot

useCases: Hold a moment of a sound as a sustained texture
Keep only the strongest partials with Gate
Inharmonic, metallic tones with Shift or Stretch
Band-limited textures with Low Cut and High Cut
Noisy, smeared versions of a sound with Randomize and Blur

name: StereoChorus
tagline: A chorus with rate, depth, centre delay, feedback and mix
description: A chorus effect built on JUCE's dsp::Chorus: a delay line whose time is swept by an LFO and blended with the dry signal. Use it to thicken guitars, keys or pads, or push the feedback and centre delay for flanger-like tones. Both channels share the same LFO, so it does not add L/R movement of its own.

features.name: LFO rate and depth
features.description: Rate runs from 0.1 to 10 Hz (skewed toward slow settings) and Depth from 0 to 1 sets how far the delay time is swept.

features.name: Centre delay
features.description: Sets the base delay from 1 to 100 ms (default 7 ms) that the LFO modulates around.

features.name: Bipolar feedback
features.description: Feedback from -0.95 to +0.95 feeds the delayed signal back with either polarity for a more resonant, comb-filtered sound.

features.name: Mix
features.description: Blends dry and chorused signal from 0 to 1 (default 0.5).

features.name: Presets
features.description: Uses the shared AudioForge preset manager to save and recall settings.

name: StringEnsemble
tagline: A Karplus-Strong plucked-string synth with up to 4 detuned strings
description: A 12-voice polyphonic synth that excites a Karplus-Strong delay-line string with a noise burst for each note, so notes behave like plucked strings that decay on their own rather than sustained bowing. Each note can stack up to four detuned strings, and the Violin, Viola, Cello and Bass types differ only in how quickly the string damps. Use it for plucked or pizzicato-style parts and string textures.

features.name: String types
features.description: Violin, Viola, Cello and Bass set progressively heavier damping in the string loop, from brighter to darker.

features.name: Ensemble size
features.description: Ensemble Size stacks one to four strings per note, detuned by 0, -5, +8 and -12 cents and averaged.

features.name: Brightness and attack
features.description: Brightness (0 to 1) lengthens and brightens the string's ring; Attack (0 to 1) sets the excitation level, the onset speed, and below 0.5 softens the noise burst.

features.name: Release
features.description: The Decay control (0 to 1) sets how quickly the note fades after note-off, with higher values giving a longer release.

features.name: Vibrato
features.description: Vibrato Depth adds up to ±2% pitch modulation at a rate of 4 to 7 Hz set by Vibrato Rate.

name: TapeDelay
tagline: A delay with wow, flutter, a darkening filter and saturated feedback
description: A stereo delay of 10 ms to 2 s whose delay time is wobbled by two fixed-rate sine LFOs (wow and flutter), with a one-pole low-pass on the repeats and tanh saturation in the feedback path. Use it for echoes that drift in pitch and get darker and softer as they repeat. It does not model a tape transport beyond those stages.

features.name: Delay time and feedback
features.description: Time runs from 10 to 2000 ms (default 500 ms) and Feedback from 0 to 0.95.

features.name: Wow and flutter
features.description: Wow adds up to ±15 ms of delay-time modulation at 0.5 Hz and Flutter up to ±5 ms at 6 Hz, each scaled 0 to 1.

features.name: Darkening repeats
features.description: A fixed one-pole low-pass filter on the delayed signal rolls off highs, and because it sits inside the loop each repeat gets darker.

features.name: Feedback saturation
features.description: Saturation (0 to 1) drives a tanh curve on the signal fed back into the delay line, softening and compressing loud repeats.

features.name: Mix
features.description: Blends dry and delayed signal from 0 to 1 (default 0.5).

name: TomSynth
tagline: A synthesized tom drum: pitched sine body with a pitch drop and noise
description: A tom drum voice made from a sine oscillator with a decaying amplitude envelope, a fast downward pitch sweep and a short noise burst, followed by fixed low-pass and high-pass filters. Every MIDI note plays the same tom at the Pitch setting, so you tune it with the knob rather than the keyboard; velocity sets the level. Use it for programmed tom fills or as a basis for electronic percussion.

features.name: Body pitch
features.description: Pitch sets the sine body frequency from 40 to 300 Hz (default 90 Hz); the note number is ignored.

features.name: Pitch drop
features.description: Pitch Env (0 to 3) and Bend (0 to 1) together set how far above the base pitch each hit starts before falling back over about 50 ms.

features.name: Decay
features.description: Sets the body's exponential decay from 0.05 to 2 seconds.

features.name: Noise attack
features.description: Noise (0 to 1) mixes in a white-noise burst that dies away in about 20 ms, adding stick attack.

features.name: Four-voice playback
features.description: Up to four overlapping hits ring out at once, each a one-shot that plays to the end of its decay regardless of note-off.

name: TremoloVibrato
tagline: Tremolo or vibrato from one LFO with sine, triangle or square shapes
description: A modulation effect with two modes: Tremolo varies the volume and Vibrato varies the pitch by sweeping a short delay line. Both use the same LFO, waveform and depth controls. Use it for amp-style pulsing, choppy square-wave gating, or wavering pitch on guitars, keys and synths.

features.name: Two modes
features.description: Tremolo scales the level between full and (1 - Depth); Vibrato reads a delay line swept between about 7 and 13 ms with linear interpolation.

features.name: Three LFO waveforms
features.description: Sine, Triangle and Square shapes, with the square giving hard on/off gating in Tremolo mode.

features.name: Rate and depth
features.description: Rate runs from 0.1 to 20 Hz (default 5 Hz) and Depth from 0 to 1.

features.name: Mix
features.description: Blends the dry and modulated signal from 0 to 1 (default fully wet).

name: VintageCompressor
tagline: A soft-knee compressor with VCA, FET and Opto timing modes
description: A stereo-linked peak compressor with threshold, ratio, soft knee, attack, release, makeup gain and a dry/wet mix for parallel compression. The VCA, FET and Opto modes only rescale the attack and release times; there is no saturation or other analog-modelling stage. Use it for general bus, drum or instrument compression.

features.name: Timing modes
features.description: VCA uses the attack and release as set, FET halves the attack and shortens release to 70%, and Opto doubles the attack and lengthens release to 150%.

features.name: Core controls
features.description: Threshold -60 to 0 dB, Ratio 1:1 to 20:1, Attack 0.1 to 100 ms and Release 10 to 1000 ms.

features.name: Soft knee
features.description: Knee from 0 to 12 dB eases the transition into compression around the threshold.

features.name: Makeup and mix
features.description: Makeup adds 0 to 24 dB after compression, and Mix (0 to 1) blends in the uncompressed signal for parallel compression.

features.name: Gain reduction meter
features.description: The editor shows the current gain reduction, detected from the louder of the two channels.

name: Vocal Compressor
tagline: A vocal compressor with RMS or peak detection and a parallel blend
description: A stereo-linked compressor aimed at vocals, with a choice of RMS (512-sample window) or peak level detection, manual makeup gain and a parallel mix control. Use it to even out a vocal's level, or blend in the dry signal for parallel compression that keeps the transients.

features.name: RMS or peak detection
features.description: RMS mode averages the level over a 512-sample window for smoother gain changes; Peak mode follows the instantaneous level.

features.name: Core controls
features.description: Threshold -60 to 0 dB (default -18), Ratio 1:1 to 20:1, Attack 0.1 to 100 ms and Release 10 to 1000 ms.

features.name: Makeup gain
features.description: Manual makeup from -12 to +24 dB applied to the compressed signal.

features.name: Parallel mix
features.description: Parallel Mix from 0 to 100% blends the uncompressed input back in; 0% is fully compressed.

features.name: Level readouts
features.description: The editor shows gain reduction and output level for each block.

name: Vocal DeEsser
tagline: A broadband de-esser keyed from a tunable 4-10 kHz sidechain
description: A de-esser that listens to a band-passed copy of the signal and turns the whole signal down when that band crosses the threshold. Because the gain reduction is applied to the full signal rather than only the high frequencies, it ducks the entire vocal briefly on each 's' or 'sh'. Use it to tame harsh sibilance on vocals or spoken word.

features.name: Tunable detection band
features.description: Frequency sets the sidechain band-pass centre from 4 to 10 kHz (default 7 kHz), and Bandwidth (0.5 to 4) widens it.

features.name: Threshold and ratio
features.description: Threshold -60 to 0 dB and Ratio 1:1 to 10:1 set when and how hard sibilant peaks are reduced.

features.name: Fast timing
features.description: Attack 0.1 to 10 ms and Release 10 to 500 ms control how quickly reduction starts and recovers.

features.name: Mix
features.description: Blends the processed and dry signal from 0 to 100%.

features.name: Gain reduction readout
features.description: The editor shows the largest gain reduction in each block.

name: Vocal Doubler
tagline: Up to four delayed, detuned, panned copies of a vocal
description: A doubler that builds one to four extra voices from the input, each with its own timing offset, small pitch offset and pan position, filtered and mixed back with the dry signal. It is meant for widening a lead vocal or faking a double-tracked part. The per-voice delay read position does not yet track the input correctly, so the voices currently come out as a stepped, held version of the input rather than a clean double.

features.name: Voices and width
features.description: Voices sets one to four copies, spread evenly across the stereo field by Stereo Width (0 to 100%) with constant-power panning.

features.name: Timing and pitch offsets
features.description: Timing Shift (0 to 30 ms) and Pitch Variation (0 to 20 cents) are scaled up per voice, with pitch offsets alternating sharp and flat.

features.name: Humanize
features.description: Humanize (0 to 100%) adds a slow LFO wobble to each voice's delay and a small random pitch jitter.

features.name: Voice filtering
features.description: A high-pass (20 to 500 Hz) and low-pass (2 to 20 kHz) filter shape the doubled voices only.

features.name: Mix and output gain
features.description: Mix blends dry and doubled signal (0 to 100%), and Output Gain trims the doubles by -12 to +12 dB.

name: Vocal Harmonizer
tagline: Up to four pitch-shifted voices at fixed intervals, each panned
description: A harmonizer that adds one to four voices, each set to a fixed interval of -24 to +24 semitones and its own pan position, then filtered and mixed with the dry signal. The Scale setting snaps each interval to the nearest step of the chosen scale; it does not detect the sung note. The pitch shifter is a single delay-line read without crossfading and does not yet produce the set intervals correctly, and the Formant Shift control is a placeholder that does nothing.

features.name: Four interval voices
features.description: Voices sets how many of the four voices play; each has a Pitch control from -24 to +24 semitones (defaults +3, +7, +12, -12).

features.name: Per-voice panning
features.description: Each voice has a Pan control from -100 to +100 with constant-power panning.

features.name: Scale snapping
features.description: Twelve scale choices (Chromatic, Major, Minor, the modes, Harmonic Minor, Melodic Minor, Pentatonic) round each voice's interval to a scale step.

features.name: Voice filtering
features.description: A high-pass (20 to 500 Hz) and low-pass (2 to 20 kHz) filter shape the harmony voices only.

features.name: Mix and output gain
features.description: Mix blends dry and harmony signal (0 to 100%), and Output Gain trims the harmonies by -12 to +12 dB.

name: Vocoder
tagline: A channel vocoder: audio input shapes a MIDI-played sawtooth carrier
description: A filter-bank vocoder that splits the audio input (the modulator) into 8 to 32 band-pass bands spaced from 100 Hz to 8 kHz, follows each band's level, and applies those levels to the same bands of an internal sawtooth carrier played from MIDI notes. It is built as an instrument that also takes audio input, so the host has to route a voice or other signal into it while you play notes. The Formant Shift control is stored but not used by the DSP.

features.name: MIDI-played carrier
features.description: Up to eight simultaneous MIDI notes each play a sawtooth, scaled by velocity and by Carrier Level (0 to 1).

features.name: Band count
features.description: Bands sets 8 to 32 log-spaced band-pass filters (Q 5); filter frequencies are only recalculated when playback is prepared.

features.name: Envelope timing
features.description: Attack (1 to 100 ms) and Release (10 to 500 ms) set how quickly each band follows the modulator.

features.name: Modulator level and mix
features.description: Modulator Level scales the vocoded output, and Mix blends it with the dry input (default fully wet).

features.name: Band level display
features.description: The editor draws a bar for each band's envelope level, updated 30 times a second.

name: WaveShaper

parameters.name: Shape
parameters.range: Soft Clip, Hard Clip, Tanh, Cubic, Asymmetric

tagline: Waveshaping distortion with five curves and a tone filter
description: A waveshaper with five transfer curves, drive up to 11x, dry/wet mix, a low-pass tone filter and output gain. A display draws the selected curve, and a 20 Hz high-pass removes DC from the output.

features.name: Five shapes
features.description: Soft Clip, Hard Clip, Tanh, Cubic and Asymmetric

features.name: Drive
features.description: 0% to 100%, multiplying the input by 1x to 11x before shaping

features.name: Curve display
features.description: Draws the selected transfer curve and redraws when you change the shape

features.name: Mix
features.description: 0% (dry) to 100% (shaped) for parallel distortion

features.name: Tone
features.description: 12 dB/octave low-pass from 500 Hz to 20 kHz after the shaper; off at 100%

features.name: Output and meters
features.description: Output gain -12 dB to +12 dB, with input and output peak readouts updated 30 times a second

useCases: Gentle saturation - Soft Clip with low drive (10-30%)
Hard digital clipping - Hard Clip with high drive
Smooth saturation - Tanh with medium drive (40-60%)
Even-harmonic colour - Asymmetric mode, where the two halves of the wave clip differently
Parallel distortion - Mix around 50%
Darker distortion - lower Tone to roll off the highs the shaper adds

algorithms.name: Soft Clip
algorithms.description: Straight below 1.0, then bends over smoothly toward ±1.5, meeting the straight part with the same slope

algorithms.name: Hard Clip
algorithms.description: Clamps the signal at ±1
algorithms.code: return clamp(input, -1.0, 1.0);

algorithms.name: Tanh Saturation
algorithms.description: Hyperbolic tangent curve
algorithms.code: return tanh(input);  // Approaches ±1 asymptotically

algorithms.name: Cubic Waveshaping
algorithms.description: x - x³/3, which adds odd harmonics; past |x| = 1 the curve turns back down, so high drive folds the wave

algorithms.name: Asymmetric Waveshaping
algorithms.description: Different curves for positive and negative halves, which adds even harmonics
algorithms.code:
if (input > 0.0)
    return tanh(input * 1.5) * 0.85;  // Harder positive
else
    return tanh(input * 0.8) * 0.95;  // Softer negative

name: WavetableSynth
tagline: 8-voice wavetable synth with 32 tables and an enveloped filter
description: An 8-voice synth that reads from 32 built-in single-cycle wavetables, from sine and saw to formant, bell and noise. One Position control moves through the tables, crossfading between neighbours, into a multi-mode filter with its own envelope and an amp envelope.

features.name: 32 wavetables
features.description: Basic waves, harmonic series, pulses, saw variants, digital, formant, vowel, bell, glass, organ, noise, chip and pad tables, generated in code

features.name: Wavetable Position
features.description: 0 to 1 across all 32 tables, interpolating between the two nearest

features.name: Multi-mode filter
features.description: Low-pass, high-pass, band-pass or notch; cutoff 20 Hz to 20 kHz, resonance 0.5 to 10

features.name: Filter envelope
features.description: Its own ADSR, adding up to 10 kHz to the cutoff, scaled by Env Amount

features.name: Amp envelope and velocity
features.description: ADSR with attack and decay up to 2 s and release up to 5 s; velocity sets the note level

features.name: 8-voice polyphony
features.description: Eight voices through the shared AudioForge voice manager

useCases: Pads - a soft table with slow attack and release
Leads - a bright table with a resonant low-pass and a short filter envelope
Bass - a saw or pulse table with the cutoff low and a snappy filter envelope
Exploring timbre - sweep Position while holding a note

name: XY Pad Controller
tagline: A two-axis pad that sends MIDI CCs as you drag it
description: An on-screen XY pad that sends two MIDI control change messages, one for each axis, on a chosen channel whenever you click or drag in it. Use it to control filter cutoff, expression or any mapped parameter on a downstream instrument with one gesture. It is built as an audio effect with MIDI output (not a MIDI effect), it silences any audio passing through it, and CCs are only sent from mouse movement in the open editor, not from host automation of the X and Y parameters.

features.name: XY pad
features.description: Dragging the ball sets X and Y from 0 to 1, shown on a grid with a live coordinate readout.

features.name: Assignable CC numbers
features.description: X CC and Y CC choose controllers 1 to 127 (defaults CC 1 mod wheel and CC 11 expression).

features.name: MIDI channel
features.description: Sends on any channel from 1 to 16.

features.name: Saved position
features.description: X Position and Y Position are host parameters, so the pad position is saved with the session and restored when the editor opens.
